newsitem.title: CHILE: Endesa brings Pangue dam into operation.
newsitem.headline: Endesa brings Pangue dam into operation.

text.p: Chilean electricity giant Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa) said it brought its Pangue hydro-electric plant in southern Chile into operation in late October -- two months earlier than planned.
The company started up the plant's first generating unit, which has a capacity of 225 megawatts, on October 31, said the firm in a statement to the Securities Superintendency.
The second unit should be brought on-line towards the end of the year, it said.
The early startup at Pangue will help reduce the effects of a severe drough which has sharply reduced water levels in dams in central Chile.
"This (startup) will ensure electricity supplies for the country and minimize the effect of the drought," said the statement.
Pangue, which costs $450 million to build, spans the Bio Bio River in the cool, forested Eighth Region.
